records.prompt: Let \(R\) be the region bounded by \(y=\sqrt{x}\) and \(y=x/2\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=4\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Cross sections perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis are squares. Find the volume.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Write, but do not evaluate, an integral for the volume when \(R\) is rotated about \(y=2\).

records.prompt: Let \(f\) be twice differentiable on \(-1.2<x<3.2\), with \(f(1)=2\). The supplied graph of \(f'\) crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\), has \(f'(1)=-4\), and has a horizontal tangent at \(x=2\). Let \(g(x)=e^{f(x)}\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write the tangent line to \(g\) at \(x=1\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find all local maxima of \(g\). Justify.
parts.answer: Because \(e^{f(x)}>0\), the sign of \(g'\) is the sign of \(f'\). The graph of \(f'\) changes from positive to negative at \(\boxed{x=-1}\), so this is the only local maximum.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Is \(g''(-1)\) positive, negative, or zero? Justify.
parts.answer:
\[
g''=e^f\left[(f')^2+f''\right].
\]
At \(x=-1\), \(f'(-1)=0\), while the graph of \(f'\) is decreasing, so \(f''(-1)<0\). Hence \(\boxed{g''(-1)<0}\).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of \(g'\) on \([1,3]\).

records.prompt:
A particle has differentiable velocity \(v(t)\), with the supplied table
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}
t&0&8&20&25&32&40\\\hline
v(t)&3&5&-10&-8&-4&7
\end{array}
\]
where time is in seconds and velocity in metres per second. The initial position is \(x(0)=7\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain \(\int_{20}^{40}v(t)dt\), and approximate it with the trapezoidal rule.
parts.answer:
The integral is the particle's displacement from \(t=20\) to \(t=40\). The trapezoidal estimate is
\[
5\frac{-10-8}{2}+7\frac{-8-4}{2}+8\frac{-4+7}{2}=-45-42+12=\boxed{-75\ \text{m}}.
\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Suppose acceleration is positive for \(0<t<8\). Explain why the position at \(t=8\) must exceed \(30\) metres.
parts.answer: Positive acceleration makes \(v(t)>v(0)=3\) for \(0<t<8\). Therefore \(x(8)-x(0)=\int_0^8v(t)dt>24\). Since \(x(0)=7\), \(\boxed{x(8)>31>30}\).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: In which listed subintervals must the particle change direction?
parts.answer: By continuity, a sign change in the table forces a zero of velocity. Thus direction must change in \(\boxed{(8,20)\text{ and }(32,40)}\).
